result:
If I could change the world in one fundamental way, I would eliminate the cognitive and emotional friction of "otherness"—replacing the instinctive human fear and distrust of the unfamiliar with an inherent, unshakeable capacity for radical empathy. 

If humans could genuinely feel the internal reality of another person as vividly as their own, almost every destructive dynamic on Earth would collapse. War, greed, cruelty, and prejudice rely entirely on the ability to compartmentalize and dehumanize those who are different. If that wall didn't exist, cruelty would become psychologically impossible, and cooperation would cease to be a strategy and instead become a reflex.
